newsitem.title: DUBAI: Families of British suspect nurses to visit Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Families of British suspect nurses to visit Saudi.

text.p: Relatives of two British nurses accused of killing an Australian colleague in Saudi Arabia are expected to see them in jail on Sunday, legal sources said on Thursday.

"Several family members of the nurses will arrive in Saudi Arabia on Saturday night and will visit them in jail on Sunday after Saudi authorities granted them approval to do so," they said by telephone from Saudi Arabia.
They declined further comment. The nurses' lawyer and British embassy officials were not immediately available for comment.
The family of the Australian nurse, Yvonne Gilford, 55, on Monday ruled out clemency for the two nurses, who could face public beheading if convicted of her murder.
She was stabbed four times and battered with a hammer and smothered in her dormitory at the King Fahd military medical complex in eastern Saudi on December 11.
Nurses Lucille McLauchlan, 31, and Deborah Parry, 41, have been charged with murder, but their lawyer said they had signed confessions in hope they would be sent home.
The Saudi law firm of Salah al-Hejailan said on Sunday the two women withdrew their murder confessions and retracted an earlier statement that they had had a lesbian relationship with the victim.

The penalty for murder in Saudi Arabia is beheading, but the sentence can be commuted at the request of the victim's family. The family can also ask for financial settlement instead of the death penalty.
